_meta.note: 以下 JSON 为验收官原始返回，未改动；字段超出 REVIEW-CONTRACT schema 的部分（criteria / rework_brief / escalate_question / reviewer_notes）原样保留。

criteria.evidence: I traced the old graph statically against validate(), and the trace reproduces the worker's output exactly. runs/plan-20261107-000746/GRAPH.json:6 max_agents → dag.workflow.mjs:479 BUDGET_RENAMED. GRAPH.json:207 rule names s_code.facts → regex at :437-444 matches it and froms is empty → SCOPE_RULE_UNCHECKED. GRAPH.json:190 and :237 are the same command, and integrate counts as a writer (:458) → CHECK_REUSES_WRITER_CMD (:469-471). No other err fires; for example integrate has writes, so SCOPE_UNCHECKABLE does not. Counter-evidence: after the edits at verify-findings.mjs:79-91 the worst case is 2+2+2+4+2+3+1=16 ≤ 16, and the new rule text contains no node.field reference, so errs empties out. I did not execute it; the run output is worker-side evidence.

Static trace of the positive group: allowlist = 2 writes + 1 DOC = 3. decisions/P1-x.json is not under allow_under → dropped, and since changed contains it the node fails (dag.workflow.mjs:837-849). This matches the worker's output line by line. I did not execute it.

See B1. The core property of rule B.4 (a retry must not take a later-wave node's first-call slot) has no test that tells the two behaviours apart. Also SCOPE_FROM_UNKNOWN (dag.workflow.mjs:325) has no contrast case: the EXPECT table at harness.mjs:30-58 has no such entry.

The 3 FAIL lines the worker reports for mutation B match my static trace (with `>`, a's retry goes through → 4 calls, error has no max_calls). So that mutation only proves the boundary operator `>=` is watched. It does not prove the `pending` reservation term is watched. Removing `pending` would survive every test (B1). Execution not verified.
I counted the backticked codes in graph-rules.md by hand: 34, and all exist in dag.workflow.mjs. But the check is a substring match (manager.py:98), which leaves a blind spot; see N4.

manager.schema.json:22-35: budget allows only max_calls, with additionalProperties:false. :139-148 has allow_from/allow_under. :156 enum includes allow_paths. All three agree with dag.workflow.mjs:87/97/479.
dag-gate.mjs:23 reads dag.workflow.mjs at runtime, :52-62 wraps it the same way the engine does and takes the dryRun path. There is no second copy of validate.

manager.py:362-366 computes sha256 over the on-disk bytes after the final Gate. RUN.json:61 has the field. I could not recompute the hash with read-only tools, so whether the value matches is unverified.

checks=94/130/140, the mutate.mjs runs and the exit 1 path all need node/python to execute, and I did not run anything. I only confirmed the mechanisms: repair errors are written to a file and referenced by path (manager.py:347-360); GATE.json waves are derivable from GRAPH.json (003443: s_code→c_iface→{w_script,w_docs}→integ→{k_hash,k_count}, nodeCount=7).
manager.py:266-270: the drift check dies before any claude call. The boundary (catches only codes the summary invented) is disclosed honestly.
[判断类] I read the old graph myself and confirmed F1 (GRAPH.json:207 vs :178-181), F2 (:6, 7 nodes, worst case 16) and F3 (:190 == :237).
[判断类] The "weaknesses" section omits that the egress check fails open and can be bypassed (B2). DELIVERY-step1.md:13 states it as a "hard block".

"The rules did not hurt the graph pass rate" is a claim about a rate. With n=1 and only one observation category (D2), it reaches at most E1, so the E2 label is overstated. Also, the brief's C6 is not the same criterion as TASK-rules.md:60 C6 (schema consistency).

blocking.what: The tests for rule B's budget reservation cannot distinguish 'reservation exists' from 'reservation does not exist', so the E3 claim for this executable item is not met.
blocking.why: The whole point of reservation is the F2 scenario: a retry must not take the first-call slot of a node in a later wave. harness.mjs:352-373 puts a, b and c in the same wave 0. Under microtask ordering, b and c both make their first calls before a sees its null result. So at the retry decision pendingFirst()=0, and `started + pending >= maxCalls` (dag.workflow.mjs:929) reduces to `started >= maxCalls`. If you delete `pending` entirely, r12 and r12b both stay green. The F2 positive group in verify-findings.mjs:137-151 uses max_calls=16, used 8/16, so the cap never binds. The first-call guard at :927 can never trigger, because the Gate already rejects nodes > cap at :494. Mutation B only covers the `>=` boundary. The mechanism itself reads correctly, but the reservation term has no counter-evidence anywhere in the test suite.
blocking.evidence: dag.workflow.mjs:778, :924-934, :494; harness.mjs:352-373; verify-findings.mjs:79, :137-151; DELIVERY-rules.md:130 (claims E3 with counter-evidence = mutation >=→>)

blocking.what: The egress check is not a hard block. It is skipped if the script is missing, it can be bypassed with a switch, manager.py has no check at all, and both evidence runs called manager.py directly.
blocking.why: This violates the hard rule in AGENTS.md (must be READY before running claude; exit 4 means stop) and DESIGN §8 Step 1 / TASK-step1.md:20 ('must be READY before the call'). DELIVERY-step1.md:13 and AGENTS.md both describe it as 'not READY → exit 4, claude does not run', which is false. This is the line of defence for account risk controls (same account, two exit IPs).
blocking.evidence: manager.ps1:52 + :61-63 (`Test-Path` fails → prints a warning and continues to call python → claude); manager.ps1:30/:50 `-SkipEgressCheck` (not mentioned in either DELIVERY); manager.py:289/309 calls claude with no egress check; DELIVERY-step1.md:78 the real opus run was `python scripts/manager.py ...`; runs/*/RUN.json has no record of the READY result

nonblocking.what: scopeCheck fails open when the allowlist is empty. dag.workflow.mjs:846 returns ok:null, and the node is then recorded as ok (:999 only fails on ok===false), even if changed lists arbitrary paths. This contradicts the 'fail-closed' comment at :817. It is the exact shape of w_docs in the new real graph (no writes, only allow_from), and when.exists treats [] as present (:811). harness rA3 (:343-347) only tests the case where writes exist. The downstream integ still has a scope check backed by static writes, so this is a defence-in-depth gap, not a hole.

Neither scope node in the new real graph sets allow_under (runs/plan-20261107-003443/GRAPH.json:132-138, :186-192). The dynamic allowlist is therefore entirely controlled by the flash scout, which is the security hole opus flagged in TASK-rules.md:39, and the Gate does not even warn. The positive group in verify-findings did add allow_under (:88); the real graph did not. On top of that, k_hash and k_count dropped cmd entirely and keep only asserts, so CHECK_CMD_UNVERIFIED is pushing the manager to remove executable checks to get 0 warn. The claim in DELIVERY §三 that all three spots are written correctly is overstated.

SCOPE_RULE_UNCHECKED's regex is lowercase-only (:437), and the schema id field has no pattern (manager.schema.json:50-53). Ids with uppercase, hyphens or a leading digit pass silently. A node whose id equals a filename stem (e.g. node `index` with rule text mentioning index.ts) triggers a false positive. A rule on node integ that says 'integ.changed ⊆ …' can only be fixed by deleting the text. The field half is not checked against FIELDS either, so the DELIVERY §五.3 description 'known node id + known field name' is inaccurate.

The drift check uses substring matching (manager.py:98). After v2, FROM_UNDECLARED, FROM_NOT_ANCESTOR and FROM_UNKNOWN are substrings of SCOPE_FROM_*, so deleting the original codes from the Gate would go undetected. Matches inside comments also count.
The allow_under prefix check does not collapse `..` (norm at :125). 'tests/../scripts/manager.py' passes the prefix check and enters the allowlist.

Stale references: dag-gate.mjs:8 points to dag.workflow.mjs:545/553/577 (now around 682/691/714); dag-gate.mjs:51 points to harness.mjs:64-66 (now 77-79); harness.mjs:12 says the default runs only the scenarios, but :398 defaults to --all; DELIVERY-step1.md:13 says manager.ps1 is 58 lines, the file is 67 (and TASK-rules says this round did not touch it).

Reservations are never released for nodes skipped by when, an upstream failure or abort (pendingFirst :778). Retries get refused while budget is still available. This is conservative and unsafe in no direction, but it should go in the 'weaknesses' list.

rework_brief: ① B1: add a test to harness.mjs where the reservation actually binds: a→b chain (b.after=['a']), max_calls=2, a.on_fail.retry=1, a's first call returns null. Expect a=fail (error mentions max_calls), b=ok, agents_started=2. Then do a single-variable mutation that changes dag.workflow.mjs:929 `started + pending >= maxCalls` to `started >= maxCalls`. The new test must go red (b becomes skipped) and the existing r12 should stay green; record both outputs in DELIVERY. ② B2: move the egress check into manager.py, before any call that reaches claude (skip it for offline/dry-run). Script missing or exit≠0 → exit 4 and no claude call. Remove -SkipEgressCheck from manager.ps1, or document it in DELIVERY with a reason. Write the check result (exit code + [result] line) into RUN.json. Add one offline-hook counter-test in manager-harness: point the check script at a nonexistent path → exit 4 and claude never invoked. Correct DELIVERY-step1.md:13 and the AGENTS.md wording to match the code. ③ Optional, same round: change the empty-allowlist case at :846 to return ok:false when changed is non-empty, add a counter-test for the no-writes shape, and add a SCOPE_FROM_UNKNOWN contrast case.
reviewer_notes: I used only Read/Grep/Glob. Both attempts to run node were refused by the permissions layer, and I made no changes to files. So all execution results (140/130/94, the mutation runs, the hashes) are unverified, and B1 rests on static tracing of microtask ordering plus reading the code. I read DELIVERY-rules.md before finishing my independent pass, which reverses the order in §二; I did not open the ledger, because this unit is mandatory, not sampling.
